claim: Yerba mate (Ilex paraguariensis) is the third-most widely consumed caffeine-containing infusion worldwide.
source: Yerba mate (YM, Ilex paraguariensis) is an economically important crop marketed for the elaboration of mate, the third-most widely consumed caffeine-containing infusion worldwide.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a factual claim about the global consumption ranking of mate.

claim: The yerba mate genome assembly has a total length of 1.06 Gb.
source: Here, we report the first genome assembly of this species, which has a total length of 1.06 Gb and contains 53,390 protein-coding genes.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by sequencing data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The yerba mate genome contains 53,390 protein-coding genes.
source: Here, we report the first genome assembly of this species, which has a total length of 1.06 Gb and contains 53,390 protein-coding genes.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by genome annotation data.

claim: The large yerba mate genome size is partly due to a whole-genome duplication (Ip-α) during the early evolutionary history of Ilex.
source: Comparative analyses revealed that the large YM genome size is partly due to a whole-genome duplication (Ip-α) during the early evolutionary history of Ilex, in addition to the hexaploidization event (γ) shared by core eudicots.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by Ks distribution analysis and synteny comparisons shown in Figure 2.

claim: Yerba mate experienced the hexaploidization event (γ) shared by core eudicots.
source: Comparative analyses revealed that the large YM genome size is partly due to a whole-genome duplication (Ip-α) during the early evolutionary history of Ilex, in addition to the hexaploidization event (γ) shared by core eudicots.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by Ks distribution analysis showing a peak at ~1.4 in Figure 2B.

claim: Yerba mate has converged upon a different biochemical pathway for caffeine production compared to that of coffee and tea.
source: To our surprise, this species has converged upon a different biochemical pathway compared to that of coffee and tea.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by enzyme activity assays shown in Figure 4.

claim: Different amino acid residues facilitate a different substrate orientation in yerba mate enzymes compared to coffee enzymes for efficient methylation.
source: The structure reveals that convergent solutions have evolved for substrate positioning because different amino acid residues facilitate a different substrate orientation such that efficient methylation occurs in the independently evolved enzymes in YM and coffee.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by the crystal structure analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: Phylogenomic constraint limits the genes coopted for convergence of caffeine biosynthesis.
source: While our results show phylogenomic constraint limits the genes coopted for convergence of caffeine biosynthesis, the X-ray diffraction data suggest structural constraints are minimal for the convergent evolution of individual reactions.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by synteny analysis shown in Figure 8.

claim: Structural constraints are minimal for the convergent evolution of individual caffeine biosynthesis reactions.
source: While our results show phylogenomic constraint limits the genes coopted for convergence of caffeine biosynthesis, the X-ray diffraction data suggest structural constraints are minimal for the convergent evolution of individual reactions.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by crystal structure data showing different residues achieving similar catalytic outcomes.

claim: Ilex paraguariensis is a diploid species with 2n = 2x = 40 chromosomes.
source: One of the few species of economic importance for which no genomic data exist is Ilex paraguariensis var. paraguariensis A. St. Hilaire (Aquifoliaceae), colloquially known as yerba mate (YM), which is a caffeinated diploid tree-species (2n = 2x = 40) endemic to the subtropical rainforests of South America (Niklas, 1987).
evidence: This is directly stated in the introduction with a citation to support the chromosome count.

claim: Ilex paraguariensis is endemic to the subtropical rainforests of South America.
source: One of the few species of economic importance for which no genomic data exist is Ilex paraguariensis var. paraguariensis A. St. Hilaire (Aquifoliaceae), colloquially known as yerba mate (YM), which is a caffeinated diploid tree-species (2n = 2x = 40) endemic to the subtropical rainforests of South America (Niklas, 1987).
evidence: This is directly stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Argentina is responsible for 80% of worldwide yerba mate production.
source: Approximately 300,000 ha are cultivated with this tree crop, with Argentina responsible for 80% of worldwide production (Heck and de Mejia, 2007).
evidence: This is directly stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Approximately 300,000 hectares are cultivated with yerba mate.
source: Approximately 300,000 ha are cultivated with this tree crop, with Argentina responsible for 80% of worldwide production (Heck and de Mejia, 2007).
evidence: This is directly stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Mate infusion has antioxidant effects in humans.
source: The mate infusion has been shown to have numerous beneficial effects in humans including as an antioxidant (Sánchez Boado et al., 2015; Gugliucci, 1996; Vieira et al., 2010), antidiabetic (Kang et al., 2012; Ríos et al., 2015), as well as central nervous system stimulant (Santos et al., 2015), among others.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations supporting the claim.

claim: Mate infusion has antidiabetic effects in humans.
source: The mate infusion has been shown to have numerous beneficial effects in humans including as an antioxidant (Sánchez Boado et al., 2015; Gugliucci, 1996; Vieira et al., 2010), antidiabetic (Kang et al., 2012; Ríos et al., 2015), as well as central nervous system stimulant (Santos et al., 2015), among others.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the claim.

claim: Mate infusion acts as a central nervous system stimulant in humans.
source: The mate infusion has been shown to have numerous beneficial effects in humans including as an antioxidant (Sánchez Boado et al., 2015; Gugliucci, 1996; Vieira et al., 2010), antidiabetic (Kang et al., 2012; Ríos et al., 2015), as well as central nervous system stimulant (Santos et al., 2015), among others.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: Three other Ilex genome sequences have been recently released.
source: Despite the recent release of three other Ilex genome sequences (Kong et al., 2022; Xu et al., 2022; Yao et al., 2022), none of the species produce caffeine, making the genetic basis for convergent evolution of this trait in YM unclear.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to the three genome papers.

claim: None of the three recently sequenced Ilex species produce caffeine.
source: Despite the recent release of three other Ilex genome sequences (Kong et al., 2022; Xu et al., 2022; Yao et al., 2022), none of the species produce caffeine, making the genetic basis for convergent evolution of this trait in YM unclear.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Caffeine has independently evolved at least six times across angiosperms.
source: Caffeine (CF) is a xanthine alkaloid that has independently evolved no less than six times across angiosperms and has implications for pollination, insect defence, and allelopathy (Anaya et al., 2006; Stevenson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the claim.

claim: Caffeine has implications for pollination, insect defence, and allelopathy.
source: Caffeine (CF) is a xanthine alkaloid that has independently evolved no less than six times across angiosperms and has implications for pollination, insect defence, and allelopathy (Anaya et al., 2006; Stevenson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the claim.

claim: In Theobroma, Paullinia, and Citrus, sequential methylation of xanthine, 1- and/or 3-methylxanthine, and either theophylline or theobromine leads to caffeine.
source: Within the Rosid genera Theobroma, Paullinia, and Citrus, sequential methylation of xanthine (X), 1- and/or 3-methylxanthine (1X, 3X) and, finally, either theophylline (TP) or theobromine (TB) leads to caffeine (Huang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the pathway.

claim: In Coffea and Camellia, sequential methylation of xanthosine, 7-methylxanthine, and theobromine yields caffeine.
source: In contrast, the Asterids, Coffea and Camellia, appear to sequentially methylate xanthosine (XR), 7-methylxanthine (7X), and theobromine (TB) to yield caffeine (Ashihara et al., 1996; Suzuki and Takahashi, 1976; Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations and reference to Figure 1.

claim: Xanthine methyltransferase (XMT) is used by Citrus and Coffea for caffeine biosynthesis.
source: Regardless of which pathway is utilized, species differ in terms of which SABATH enzyme family members were convergently recruited to synthesize caffeine: xanthine methyltransferase (XMT) is used by Citrus and Coffea while the paralogous caffeine synthase (CS) is used by Camellia, Theobroma, and Paullinia (Huang et al., 2016; Kato et al., 1996; Uefuji et al., 2003; Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations and reference to Figure 1.

claim: Caffeine synthase (CS) is used by Camellia, Theobroma, and Paullinia for caffeine biosynthesis.
source: Regardless of which pathway is utilized, species differ in terms of which SABATH enzyme family members were convergently recruited to synthesize caffeine: xanthine methyltransferase (XMT) is used by Citrus and Coffea while the paralogous caffeine synthase (CS) is used by Camellia, Theobroma, and Paullinia (Huang et al., 2016; Kato et al., 1996; Uefuji et al., 2003; Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations and reference to Figure 1.

claim: Different amino acid replacements to homologous regions of CS and XMT enzymes govern the evolution of substrate preference switches.
source: Convergence appears to also extend to the mutational level, since different amino acid replacements to homologous regions of CS and XMT enzymes appear to govern the evolution of substrate preference switches (O'Donnell et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: The yerba mate genome was sequenced using Illumina and PacBio sequencing technologies.
source: The YM genome was sequenced combining Illumina and PacBio sequencing technologies.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the sequencing approach.

claim: Illumina sequencing generated approximately 263.2 Gb of short reads from various DNA fragment sizes.
source: With Illumina sequencing, we generated ~263.2 Gb of short reads from various DNA fragment sizes (350 bp, 550 bp, 3 kbp, 8 kbp, and 12 kbp), while with PacBio sequencing, we generated ~77.5 Gb of long reads.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Table 1.

claim: PacBio sequencing generated approximately 77.5 Gb of long reads.
source: With Illumina sequencing, we generated ~263.2 Gb of short reads from various DNA fragment sizes (350 bp, 550 bp, 3 kbp, 8 kbp, and 12 kbp), while with PacBio sequencing, we generated ~77.5 Gb of long reads.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Table 1.

claim: The total assembly length was approximately 1.06 Gb and consisted of 10,611 scaffolds (≥1 kb).
source: The total assembly length was ~1.06 Gb and consisted of 10,611 scaffolds (≥1 kb) with an N50 length of ~510.8 kb (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Table 2.

claim: The N50 length of the assembly is approximately 510.8 kb.
source: The total assembly length was ~1.06 Gb and consisted of 10,611 scaffolds (≥1 kb) with an N50 length of ~510.8 kb (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Table 2.

claim: 99.3% of transcriptome reads mapped to the assembly.
source: To assess the completeness of the genome, we aligned the available YM transcriptome reads (Acevedo et al., 2019; Debat et al., 2014; Fay et al., 2018) and the YM genomic short reads generated in this study with the assembly: 99.3% of the former and 99.5% of the latter were mapped.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to the transcriptome data sources.

claim: 99.5% of genomic short reads mapped to the assembly.
source: To assess the completeness of the genome, we aligned the available YM transcriptome reads (Acevedo et al., 2019; Debat et al., 2014; Fay et al., 2018) and the YM genomic short reads generated in this study with the assembly: 99.3% of the former and 99.5% of the latter were mapped.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The GC content of the yerba mate genome assembly is 36.33%.
source: The GC content of the genome assembly was 36.33% (Table 2), similar to that of other eudicots (33.70–38.20 GC%) (Singh et al., 2016) and almost identical to that of Ilex polyneura (36.08 GC%) (Yao et al., 2022), Ilex asprella (36.25 GC%) (Kong et al., 2022), and Ilex latifolia (36.44 GC%) (Xu et al., 2022), the only three Ilex species with sequenced genomes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Table 2 and citations comparing to other species.

claim: About 64.63% of the yerba mate genome assembly is composed of repetitive sequences.
source: About 64.63% of the genome assembly was composed of repetitive sequences, of which ~36.22% were retrotransposons, ~1.80% were DNA transposons, ~0.74% were simple repeats, and ~0.15% were low complexity regions.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Table 3.

claim: Approximately 36.22% of the yerba mate genome consists of retrotransposons.
source: About 64.63% of the genome assembly was composed of repetitive sequences, of which ~36.22% were retrotransposons, ~1.80% were DNA transposons, ~0.74% were simple repeats, and ~0.15% were low complexity regions.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Table 3.

claim: Long terminal-repeat retrotransposons of the Gypsy and Copia families are the most abundant transposable elements in yerba mate.
source: Long terminal-repeat retrotransposons of the Gypsy and Copia families were the most abundant transposable elements, as observed in many sequenced plant genomes (Galindo-González et al., 2017), followed by long interspersed nuclear elements (LINEs) and hobo-Activator transposons, among others (Table 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Table 3 and a citation.

claim: A total of 53,390 protein-coding genes were predicted in the yerba mate genome.
source: A total of 53,390 protein-coding genes were predicted in the genome, with a mean coding sequence length of 3062 bp and 4.23 exons per gene.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The mean coding sequence length in yerba mate is 3062 bp.
source: A total of 53,390 protein-coding genes were predicted in the genome, with a mean coding sequence length of 3062 bp and 4.23 exons per gene.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Yerba mate genes have an average of 4.23 exons per gene.
source: A total of 53,390 protein-coding genes were predicted in the genome, with a mean coding sequence length of 3062 bp and 4.23 exons per gene.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Approximately 77.63% of predicted yerba mate genes could be annotated with GO terms, EC numbers or Pfam domains.
source: Of these, 41,483 (~77.63%) could be annotated with GO terms, EC numbers or Pfam domains.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: 4,530 non-coding RNA genes were identified in the yerba mate genome.
source: In addition, we identified 4530 non-coding RNA genes, including 2670 small nucleolar RNAs, 815 transfer RNAs, 471 ribosomal RNAs, 348 small nuclear RNAs, and 226 micro RNAs (Appendix 1, Appendix 1—tables 1–3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to appendix tables.

claim: 98% of core gene families from the KOG database are present in the yerba mate genome.
source: To further assess the completeness of the assembly, we aligned the scaffolds with the KOG (Tatusov et al., 2003) and DEG (Luo et al., 2014) databases, determining that 98% of the core gene families from the KOG database and 97.5% of the Arabidopsis thaliana DEG subset were present.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to the databases.

claim: 97.5% of the Arabidopsis thaliana DEG subset are present in the yerba mate genome.
source: To further assess the completeness of the assembly, we aligned the scaffolds with the KOG (Tatusov et al., 2003) and DEG (Luo et al., 2014) databases, determining that 98% of the core gene families from the KOG database and 97.5% of the Arabidopsis thaliana DEG subset were present.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to the databases.

claim: Approximately 96.20% of BUSCO conserved single-copy genes were retrieved from the yerba mate genome.
source: Then, we performed a Benchmarking Universal Single-Copy Orthologs (BUSCO) (Manni et al., 2021) assessment using the eudicot ODB10 database. Among 2326 conserved single-copy genes, ~96.20% were retrieved, of which ~78.80% were complete and single copies, ~17.40% were complete and in duplicates, ~3.10% were fragmented, and only ~0.70% were missing.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation to the BUSCO method.

claim: The number of estimated genes for yerba mate is higher than the approximately 39,000 reported from other Ilex species genomes.
source: The number of estimated genes for YM is higher than the ca. 39,000 reported from the genome sequences of other Ilex species (Kong et al., 2022; Xu et al., 2022; Yao et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to other Ilex genome papers.

claim: The higher gene number in yerba mate could be partly due to its larger genome size relative to other Ilex species.
source: This could be at least partly due to the larger genome size of YM as estimated from flow cytometry relative to the other species (Gottlieb and Poggio, 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: The Ks distribution of yerba mate paralogues revealed a significant peak with a median Ks value of approximately 0.37.
source: The Ks distribution of YM paralogues (Figure 2B) revealed a significant peak with a median Ks value of ~0.37, not shared with the rest of the eudicot genomes analysed (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The Ilex-specific polyploidization event (Ip-α) is confirmed by a Ks peak with median value of approximately 0.37.
source: This confirms the lineage-specific polyploidization event (Ip-α) previously reported in Ilex (One Thousand Plant Transcriptomes Initiative, 2019; Xu et al., 2022; Yao et al., 2022; Zhang et al., 2020b), in addition to the shared ancestral WGT-γ which is indicated by a median Ks value of ~1.4 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations and reference to Figure 2B.

claim: The shared ancestral WGT-γ is indicated by a median Ks value of approximately 1.4.
source: This confirms the lineage-specific polyploidization event (Ip-α) previously reported in Ilex (One Thousand Plant Transcriptomes Initiative, 2019; Xu et al., 2022; Yao et al., 2022; Zhang et al., 2020b), in addition to the shared ancestral WGT-γ which is indicated by a median Ks value of ~1.4 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: There are 2:1 syntenic depth ratios between the yerba mate genome and the coffee and grape genomes.
source: A WGD in the common ancestor of Ilex species is further supported by 2:1 syntenic depth ratios between the YM genome and the coffee and grape genomes, which did not experience additional duplication events after the ancestral WGT-γ (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Coffee and grape genomes did not experience additional duplication events after the ancestral WGT-γ.
source: A WGD in the common ancestor of Ilex species is further supported by 2:1 syntenic depth ratios between the YM genome and the coffee and grape genomes, which did not experience additional duplication events after the ancestral WGT-γ (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The age of the Ip-α WGD event was estimated between 48.75 and 69.63 Ma using the plastid genome phylogeny.
source: With the former phylogeny, we estimated the age of the WGD event between 48.75 and 69.63 Ma while, with the latter, divergence was estimated at 49.43 and 70.62 Ma (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: The age of the Ip-α WGD event was estimated between 49.43 and 70.62 Ma using the nuclear genome phylogeny.
source: With the former phylogeny, we estimated the age of the WGD event between 48.75 and 69.63 Ma while, with the latter, divergence was estimated at 49.43 and 70.62 Ma (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: The age estimates for Ip-α are consistent with previous estimates and validate the age near the origin of Ilex, estimated between 43 and 89 Ma.
source: Both estimates are consistent with that of Zhang et al., 2020a and validate the age of Ip-α near the origin of Ilex, which is estimated between 43 and 89 Ma (Yao et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: There are 28 full-length SABATH genes in the yerba mate genome.
source: There appear to be 28 full-length SABATH genes in YM that encode members of the functionally diverse clades of the family, including SAMT (Ross et al., 1999) and JMT (Seo et al., 2001), among others (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations and reference to Figure 3A.

claim: The yerba mate genome contains three recently and tandemly duplicated genes that encode CS-type enzymes: IpCS1, IpCS2, and IpCS3.
source: Our phylogenetic analysis showed that although the YM genome does not appear to encode XMT-type caffeine-producing enzymes like Coffea and Citrus, it does contain three recently and tandemly duplicated genes that encode CS-type enzymes, IpCS1, IpCS2, and IpCS3 (Figure 3A, C, Appendix 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 3A and 3C.

claim: The yerba mate genome does not encode XMT-type caffeine-producing enzymes like Coffea and Citrus.
source: Our phylogenetic analysis showed that although the YM genome does not appear to encode XMT-type caffeine-producing enzymes like Coffea and Citrus, it does contain three recently and tandemly duplicated genes that encode CS-type enzymes, IpCS1, IpCS2, and IpCS3 (Figure 3A, C, Appendix 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: IpCS1-3 are 86-91% identical at the amino acid level.
source: The duplicated IpCS1–3 are 86–91% identical at the amino acid level and are expressed at highest levels in caffeine-accumulating tissue (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: IpCS1-3 are expressed at highest levels in caffeine-accumulating tissue.
source: The duplicated IpCS1–3 are 86–91% identical at the amino acid level and are expressed at highest levels in caffeine-accumulating tissue (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: IpCS1-3 are of recent origin, as non-caffeine accumulating Ilex species only have a single gene or gene fragment in the syntenic region.
source: IpCS1–3 also appear to be of recent origin, since non-caffeine accumulating Ilex species only have a single gene or gene fragment in the syntenic region (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: IpCS1 primarily methylates xanthine to catalyse the formation of 3-methylxanthine.
source: One enzyme, IpCS1, appears to primarily methylate X to catalyse the formation of 3X (Figure 4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4.

claim: IpCS2 shows activity only with 3-methylxanthine to produce theobromine.
source: A second enzyme, IpCS2, shows activity only with 3X to produce TB, while a third enzyme, IpCS3, exhibits a preference to methylate TB to form CF (Figure 4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4.

claim: IpCS3 exhibits a preference to methylate theobromine to form caffeine.
source: A second enzyme, IpCS2, shows activity only with 3X to produce TB, while a third enzyme, IpCS3, exhibits a preference to methylate TB to form CF (Figure 4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4.

claim: The three IpCS enzymes collectively catalyse a complete pathway from xanthine to caffeine.
source: Thus, collectively, these three enzymes appear capable of catalysing a complete pathway from xanthine to caffeine.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the enzyme activity data.

claim: The apparent KM for the preferred substrates of all three IpCS enzymes ranges from 85 to 197 μM.
source: The apparent KM for the preferred substrates of all three enzymes ranges from 85 to 197 μM, and the kcat/KM estimates are comparable to those determined for other caffeine biosynthetic enzymes (O'Donnell et al., 2021; Table 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Table 4 and a citation.

claim: 14C xanthine tracer studies in young leaf segments of I. paraguariensis showed radioactivity in 3-methylxanthine and theobromine in addition to caffeine.
source: Further evidence for this biosynthetic pathway has been reported by 14C xanthine tracer studies in young leaf segments of I. paraguariensis that showed radioactivity in 3X and TB in addition to CF (Yin et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: A pathway from X→3X→TB→CF has been reported for Theobroma and Paullinia using CS-type SABATH enzymes.
source: A pathway from X→3X→TB→CF has also been reported for Theobroma and Paullinia using CS-type SABATH enzymes (Huang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: Ilex, Theobroma, and Paullinia convergently recruited CS genes that independently duplicated and evolved to encode enzymes with similar substrate preferences to catalyse a common pathway to caffeine.
source: The fact that Ilex, Theobroma, and Paullinia convergently recruited CS genes that independently duplicated and evolved to encode enzymes with similar substrate preferences to catalyse a common pathway to caffeine, in spite of their divergence more than 100 Ma (Yang et al., 2020), is remarkable and suggests a high degree of genetic constraint governing the repeated origin of this trait.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: Ilex, Theobroma, and Paullinia diverged more than 100 million years ago.
source: The fact that Ilex, Theobroma, and Paullinia convergently recruited CS genes that independently duplicated and evolved to encode enzymes with similar substrate preferences to catalyse a common pathway to caffeine, in spite of their divergence more than 100 Ma (Yang et al., 2020), is remarkable and suggests a high degree of genetic constraint governing the repeated origin of this trait.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: The crystal structure of IpCS3 was determined at 2.7 Å resolution.
source: We successfully crystallized and determined the 2.7 Å resolution structure of IpCS3 (PDB ID: 8UZD), that converts TB into CF.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: IpCS3 crystallizes as a holo-homodimer bound to S-adenosyl-homocysteine (SAH) and caffeine.
source: This enzyme crystallizes as a holo-homodimer, bound to both of its reaction products: S-adenosyl-homocysteine (SAH) and caffeine (Figure 6A, Table 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6A and Table 5.

claim: IpCS3 exhibits a Rossman-like fold composed of seven β-strands surrounded by five α-helices.
source: As is typical for the SABATH family of methyltransferases, IpCS3 exhibits a Rossman-like fold composed of seven β-strands surrounded by five α-helices which bind the methyl-donor S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM), as well as an α-helical cap which binds the methyl-acceptor theobromine (McCarthy and McCarthy, 2007; Petronikolou et al., 2018; Zhao et al., 2008; Zubieta et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: In both CcDXMT and IpCS3, His160/His155 and Trp161/Trp156 are conserved residues that form the active site pocket.
source: In both CcDXMT and IpCS3, there are several conserved residues, shared by nearly all SABATH enzymes (Figure 6—figure supplements 3 and 4), that form the active site pocket and appear to play important roles in binding many different substrates (Petronikolou et al., 2018; Zubieta et al., 2003). His160 and Trp161 in CcDXMT are in the same relative positions as His155 and Trp156 in IpCS3 (Figure 6B, C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations and reference to Figure 6B and 6C.

claim: In CcDXMT, His160 and Trp161 form hydrogen bonds to carbonyl O2 of theobromine when positioned for N1 methylation.
source: In CcDXMT, the NE2 of His160 and NE1 of Trp161 form hydrogen bonds to carbonyl O2 of TB when positioned for N1 methylation; yet, in the structure of IpCS3 these corresponding side chain groups form hydrogen bonds to O6 of TB.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: In IpCS3, His155 and Trp156 form hydrogen bonds to O6 of theobromine.
source: In CcDXMT, the NE2 of His160 and NE1 of Trp161 form hydrogen bonds to carbonyl O2 of TB when positioned for N1 methylation; yet, in the structure of IpCS3 these corresponding side chain groups form hydrogen bonds to O6 of TB.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The substrates in CcDXMT and IpCS3 are rotated 180° along an axis going through N1 and C4.
source: Despite these two residues being conserved for H-bonding, the substrates are rotated 180° along an axis going through N1 and C4. Thus, the conserved His and Trp residues interact with opposing carbonyls in TB/CF but still position the substrate for N1 methylation (Figure 6B, C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6B and 6C.

claim: In CcDXMT, Ser237 allows specific hydrogen bonding with N9 to position theobromine for N1 methylation.
source: Specifically, in the structure of CcDXMT, the hydroxyl group of Ser237 allows specific hydrogen bonding with N9 to position TB for N1 methylation (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6C.

claim: In IpCS3, His236 is found at the homologous position to Ser237 in CcDXMT.
source: In IpCS3, His236 is found at the homologous position in the structure.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: In IpCS3, Asn353 forms a hydrogen bond with N9 of theobromine.
source: Tyr368 of CcDXMT is found to participate in π–π interactions with the ring structure of TB Lanzarotti et al., 2020; yet in IpCS3, Asn353 is found in the homologous position and the amine forms a hydrogen bond with N9 due to its proximity within 3.2 Å, which is additionally stabilized by Asn221 and His236 (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6B.

claim: Five amino acid positions (A22G, R23C, T25S, H221N, and Y265C) are important for governing xanthine alkaloid methylation in IpCS3.
source: We chose to mutate five amino acid positions that appear to be important for governing xanthine alkaloid methylation in IpCS3 and other CS-type enzymes (Jin et al., 2016; O'Donnell et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2023; Yoneyama et al., 2006); these included A22G, R23C, T25S, H221N, and Y265C (Figure 6—figure supplements 3 and 4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: When five amino acid residues were mutated simultaneously in AncIpCS2, activity with theobromine increased dramatically relative to 3-methylxanthine and all other xanthine alkaloid substrates.
source: When we mutated all five amino acid residues simultaneously in AncIpCS2, we found that activity with TB increased dramatically relative to 3X and all other xanthine alkaloid substrates (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5A.

claim: The five mutated sites are crucial for the evolution of theobromine methylation in the history of the yerba mate lineage.
source: Thus, these five sites appear to be crucial for the evolution of TB methylation in the history of the YM lineage and further indicate that convergence of caffeine biosynthesis in different species is a result of amino acid replacements at these sites.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on mutagenesis data.

claim: IpCS1 residues W156, N221, and Y265 are positioned for hydrogen bonding with the carbonyl moieties of xanthine to position N3 for methyl transfer from SAM.
source: From our docking simulations, IpCS1 residues W156, N221, and Y265 are positioned for hydrogen bonding with the carbonyl moieties of xanthine to position N3 for methyl transfer from SAM (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 7A.

claim: In IpCS2, two hydrogen bond donors, S24 and T25, contribute to the positioning of 3-methylxanthine in the active site.
source: In the case of IpCS2, two hydrogen bond donors, S24 and T25, appear to contribute to the positioning of 3X in the active site (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 7B.

claim: Coffea lacks a CS orthologue in the syntenic region used for caffeine biosynthesis in yerba mate and Theobroma.
source: For example, in the case of the CS syntenic region used for caffeine biosynthesis in YM and Theobroma, Coffea lacks a CS orthologue and none can be detected from its genome (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 8—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Yerba mate appears to have lost any vestiges of XMT orthologues known to be responsible for caffeine biosynthesis in Coffea and Citrus.
source: Conversely, YM appears to have lost any vestiges of XMT orthologues known to be responsible for caffeine biosynthesis in Coffea and Citrus (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B–D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 8—figure supplement 1B-D.

claim: The lack of genomic potential may be seen as an evolutionary constraint to gene recruitment for caffeine biosynthesis in Coffea and yerba mate.
source: This lack of genomic potential may be seen as an evolutionary constraint to gene recruitment for caffeine biosynthesis in Coffea and YM.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the synteny data.

claim: Both CS- and XMT-type caffeine biosynthetic enzymes were present in the ancestor of core eudicots.
source: Both CS- and XMT-type caffeine biosynthetic enzymes were present in the ancestor of core eudicots but numerous apparent losses of one or the other or both has occurred during lineage diversification.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 8 and supported by synteny analysis.

claim: Numerous apparent losses of CS or XMT or both have occurred during lineage diversification.
source: Both CS- and XMT-type caffeine biosynthetic enzymes were present in the ancestor of core eudicots but numerous apparent losses of one or the other or both has occurred during lineage diversification.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 8 and shown in the figure.

claim: The caffeine-producing Coffea, Camellia, Citrus, Paullinia, and Ilex lineages each originated within only the last 10-20 million years.
source: Nonetheless, because molecular clock analyses indicate that the caffeine-producing Coffea, Camellia, Citrus, Paullinia, and Ilex lineages each originated within only the last 10–20 million years (Buerki et al., 2011; Hamon et al., 2017; Pfeil and Crisp, 2008; Yao et al., 2021; Zan et al., 2023), it suggests that the evolution of novel specialized metabolic pathways like that of caffeine can be relatively rapid.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: The evolution of novel specialized metabolic pathways like that of caffeine can be relatively rapid.
source: Nonetheless, because molecular clock analyses indicate that the caffeine-producing Coffea, Camellia, Citrus, Paullinia, and Ilex lineages each originated within only the last 10–20 million years (Buerki et al., 2011; Hamon et al., 2017; Pfeil and Crisp, 2008; Yao et al., 2021; Zan et al., 2023), it suggests that the evolution of novel specialized metabolic pathways like that of caffeine can be relatively rapid.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from molecular clock data.

claim: AncIpCS1 exhibits highest relative activity with xanthine, 3-methylxanthine, and 7-methylxanthine.
source: The ancestral enzyme, AncIpCS1, which gave rise to all three modern-day YM enzymes, exhibits highest relative activity with X, 3X, and 7X (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5A.

claim: AncIpCS1 could not produce caffeine.
source: These data demonstrate that, although AncIpCS1 could not produce caffeine, it could methylate xanthine alkaloids at 3 different positions of the planar heterocyclic ring structures and this combination of activities would have allowed for the ancestor of YM to produce a cocktail of 1X, 3X, TP, and TB by flux through multiple branches of the xanthine alkaloid biosynthetic network with a single enzyme (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5B.

claim: AncIpCS1 could methylate xanthine alkaloids at 3 different positions of the planar heterocyclic ring structures.
source: These data demonstrate that, although AncIpCS1 could not produce caffeine, it could methylate xanthine alkaloids at 3 different positions of the planar heterocyclic ring structures and this combination of activities would have allowed for the ancestor of YM to produce a cocktail of 1X, 3X, TP, and TB by flux through multiple branches of the xanthine alkaloid biosynthetic network with a single enzyme (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5B.

claim: AncIpCS2 evolved high relative activity with 7-methylxanthine to produce not just theobromine, but also paraxanthine by methylation at the N1 position.
source: However, unlike its ancestor, AncIpCS1, AncIpCS2 evolved high relative activity with 7X to produce not just TB, but also PX by methylation at the N1 position (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 5B.

claim: AncIpCS2 retained the ancestral activity of AncIpCS1 with xanthine to produce 1-methylxanthine, but also evolved the ability to methylate xanthine at the N7 position.
source: AncIpCS2 retained the ancestral activity of AncIpCS1 with xanthine to produce 1X, but also evolved the ability to methylate X at the N7 position (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 5B.

claim: AncIpCS2 retained ancestral activity with 3-methylxanthine to produce only theobromine by N7 methylation but lost the ability to methylate 3-methylxanthine at the N1 position to form theophylline.
source: This enzyme also retained ancestral activity with 3X to produce only TB by N7 methylation but lost the ability to methylate 3X at the N1 position to form TP.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The xanthine alkaloids 1-methylxanthine, 3-methylxanthine, and theophylline can bind to modern-day rat adenosine receptors.
source: It has been shown that the xanthine alkaloids, 1X, 3X, and TP, can bind to modern-day rat adenosine receptors (Daly et al., 1983).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: The modern-day CS enzymes of yerba mate evolved to catalyse a pathway from X>3X>TB>CF from ancestral biosynthetic networks of different products.
source: Not only did the modern-day CS enzymes of YM evolve to catalyse a pathway from X>3X>TB>CF from ancestral biosynthetic networks of different products, Theobroma and Paullinia also independently evolved enzymes with similar properties (Huang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: Theobroma and Paullinia independently evolved enzymes with similar properties to yerba mate CS enzymes from ancestral pathways with alternative ancestral fluxes.
source: Not only did the modern-day CS enzymes of YM evolve to catalyse a pathway from X>3X>TB>CF from ancestral biosynthetic networks of different products, Theobroma and Paullinia also independently evolved enzymes with similar properties (Huang et al., 2016). And, they did so from ancestral pathways that, like YM, had alternative ancestral fluxes (O'Donnell et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.
